comment: What the developer's recordings (the private AdrianAbbas/Samples repository: MP3s and WAVs, in its root or in folders; a file is found by its path or, if it moved, by its name anywhere under the repository) contain, from its notes.txt, checked against the audio by prepare.py. Note names: C4 = MIDI 60. 'takes' is how many times each note was played (round-robins); 0 means it varies (counted from the audio). 'pitchFrom': 'audio' (the voice): the names say what was meant, the detected pitch decides where a note is mapped (the voice files are named an octave below what was sung). Layers with the same name are one velocity layer (extra takes); 'into' copies a file's notes into several layers (the falsetto plays at every velocity); 'pick' takes a range of a file's notes ('fileTakes' in all: the banjo's 5th string file holds the soft, medium and hard hits in order). 'gainGroup': sets recorded at one gain share one gain. 'fx': the set also ships in the effect's bundle (its Atmosphere layer). Synth sweeps ('kind': 'synth'): one patch per WAV, every key of the Minilogue's 37 from lowest to highest; 'articulation' short or long (held: looped), 'patch' groups the two (one gain: same input gain per patch); pitches and octaves come from the audio (sweeps.py). 'ship': false prepares and reports a set (its notes checked) but leaves it out of index.json and the output (no instrument plays it: not loaded, not bundled).
